recipes.name: Slow Cooker Ribs
ingredients_raw: 0.5 teaspoon steak seasoning, or to taste
0.5 teaspoon garlic salt, or to taste
0.25 teaspoon ground black pepper, or to taste
0.25 teaspoon chili powder, or to taste
1 (4 pound) package boneless country-style pork ribs
2 dashes hot pepper sauce, or to taste

steps.text: Mix together steak seasoning, garlic salt, black pepper, and chili powder in a small bowl until combined.
Rub over ribs and place into the bottom of a slow cooker.
Pour in barbecue sauce, Worcestershire sauce, soy sauce, teriyaki sauce, orange juice, and hot pepper sauce. Liquid should not cover ribs completely.
Cook on Low until ribs are tender, about 8 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Slow Cooker Ribs
raw_recipe.description: These crockpot boneless ribs use a set-it-and-forget-it slow cooker recipe for tender country-style pork cooked in barbecue sauce and orange juice.

review.reviewBody: These came out really delicious. However, I only bought 2 pounds of ribs, and I needed a lot more of the dry ingredients to get a good rub. I just kept adding to the bowl - probably with a tablespoon of each dry ingredient by the end.

This was delicious! I modified slightly and made it in my Dutch oven. I had no teriyaki or garlic salt. I used garlic, a touch of honey, and liquid smoke instead. I headed the advice of others and seared the meat before cooking. To coat the ribs I mixed them in a mixing bowl. I believe I used 4 teaspoons of each dry ingredient. They cooked in the oven at 325 for roughly 3 hours.

This is the best rib recipe I have ever made. I followed the recipe exactly and added a bit of hoisin sauce and sweet chili sauce. So easy, cooked on high for 6 hours and the ribs were perfectly juicy and incredibly flavorful. This is a keeper, I will make it again!! Thank you for posting!

I did as another reviewer suggested and started with a Tablespoon on some of the ingredients. Since I don't have garlice salt on hand any longer I used 2 Tablespoons of Garlic Powder and 1 tsp of salt , 2 Tbl. of the Chili powder and the steak seasoning and 1 tsp of a fine black pepper. I acutally started off with half and when I was half way through I was out of rub so I made another batch and it was exactly enough. This is the best way to cook country style ribs I have ever tasted. Wonderful recipe. We grill baby backs on the grill and they are perfect but Country style ribs always seem to get dry and chewy. This was tender and juicy. Can't wait to eat it again. I wish there was a way to customize the recipe with the changes.

This came out perfect! I notoriously over-cook ribs and this was the first time they came out just right. I used a couple different seasonings based on what I had on hand. I left out the teriyaki sauce and put in extra orange juice. I also added some brown sugar to the mixture to give it a little sweetness. I marinated the ribs overnight in the sauce. It came out super delicious!!

Omg....so good!!! The meat just fell apart and melted in my mouth...i did use about a teaspoon full of the spices to rub on the meat and i found the liquid mixture just a little too salty for my taste...so i added some brown sugar and honey to the liquids ...i also cooked the meat on high for 3 1/2 hours and for the last 1 1/2 i turned it down to low....these were some of the best ribs ever...

We liked this. I liked the chili powder and Worcestershire sauce in it. I used Sweet Baby Ray's BBQ sauce. I didn't have teriyaki, so I left that out and used 1/2 cup pineapple juice in place of it and the OJ. I used garlic powder instead of salt to cut down on the saltiness. I finely chopped a small yellow onion and put that in too. At 8 hrs, the meat on the outer edges was getting a bit burnt and a little dry, so my crockpot only needs 6-7 hrs next time. I served mashed potatoes and used the sauce as gravy. Thanks for a great recipe I'll make again.

Delicious as written. Do not rush the cooking time. 8 hours in the slow cooker makes the difference though they seem tender at 4-5. All else is flexible. If you don’t like soy sauce, don’t use it. If you don’t have orange juice, try apple or pineapple. Etc. The rub should be a tablespoon or so of dry ingredients, four pinches isn’t enough.
these were good. however I used garlic powder instead of garlic salt & skipped the black pepper cause there was already so much salt & pepper in the steak seasoning. they turned out delicious!

These ribs were a big hit with my family. I only made a few changes. I increased the amount of rub to about 1 teaspoon of each spice, and added 1 tsp of picante smoked paprika. We like spicy dishes. Will definitely make this again.

These come out soo good. I used about a table spoon of each of the dry rub, I used Sweet Baby Ray's Hickory & Brown Sugar BBQ sauce. I added about 1/4 cup chopped onion and as a twist I spread a can of crushed pineapple over the ribs, cooked on low setting for 6 hours. just falling apart and so good. served with cheesy mashed potatoes.
Finally a recipe for ribs that tastes "marinated". Slow cooker makes clean up stress free!
Spiced it up to my tastes. Then oven baked them 350 for 20 minutes a side. To get rid of some fats. Then 6 hrs in the slow cooker on low. Delicious

My husband and I both enjoyed these pork ribs. The recipe said to cook them in the crockpot for 8 hours but ours were nice and tender after 4 hours. I made Jasmine rice and it was very good with the sauce on top. I would rate this recipe of 4.5.

I made this tonight and it was really good! I made a couple tweaks. I ended up here because I'd found pre-seasoned orange pepper country ribs at the grocery store. I thought they sounded good but wasn't quite sure what to do with them. That being said, I didn't use the rub in this recipe since they were already seasoned. I did make the sauce and made this in the pressure cooker instead of slow cook. I seared the ribs in oil before starting pressure cook mode. I used the sauce as written and cooked on high pressure for 10 minutes. They were great. I paired it with a chopped salad with grilled corn, orange bell pepper, tomato, red onion, cucumber, and a honey Dijon lime dressing. It was great.
Made it for my wife said, "it's a KEEPER!" Now, I do 95% of the cooking for our little household and while she likes most of i cook, "It's a keeper," happens about 1x a month...
Used pineapple juice and chunks(served fruit as side) not orange ju. De licious!
You need to drain off the grease or fat before putting on the barbecue sauce.

This is the second time I’ve done these. So delicious! One small issue I had was I cooked less than 4 lbs of ribs and should’ve cooked them about 6 hrs on low. They were slightly overcooked, but still delicious. I used apple cider vinegar instead of the orange juice and sliced up a sweet onion on the floor of the crockpot with the ribs on top. Another easy, but great recipe! Thanks.
